title: Impact of weather on marathon-running performance
authors: Ely MR, Cheuvront SN, Roberts WO, Montain SJ
population: Finishers at 7 major marathons (Boston, New York, Twin Cities, Grandma's, Richmond, Hartford, Vancouver) over 6-36 years each, with weather data
findings: Top males were slower than the course record by 1.7 +/- 1.5, 2.5 +/- 2.1, 3.3 +/- 2.0 and 4.5 +/- 2.3% for WBGT quartiles 5.1-10, 10.1-15, 15.1-20 and 20.1-25 C; Q4 vs Q1/Q2 and Q3 vs Q1 differed significantly (P < 0.05).
Top women followed a similar trend (3.2, 3.2, 3.8, 5.4%) but quartile differences were not statistically significant.
The 25th-, 50th-, 100th- and 300th-place finishers slowed more than faster runners as WBGT increased.
Conclusion: progressive slowing from 5 to 25 C WBGT for men and women of wide-ranging abilities, more so for slower populations.
Races were grouped by WBGT quartile: Q1 5.1-10, Q2 10.1-15, Q3 15.1-20, Q4 20.1-25 C.
Top male finishers were slower than the course record by 1.7 +/- 1.5, 2.5 +/- 2.1, 3.3 +/- 2.0 and 4.5 +/- 2.3% in Q1-Q4; Q4 differed from Q1 and Q2, and Q3 from Q1 (P < 0.05).
Top women followed a similar trend (3.2 +/- 4.9, 3.2 +/- 2.9, 3.8 +/- 3.2, 5.4 +/- 4.1% in Q1-Q4) but quartile differences were not statistically significant.
The 25th-, 50th-, 100th- and 300th-place finishers slowed more than faster runners as WBGT rose.
Equivalence testing around a 1% indifference threshold suggested potentially important changes among quartiles for all runners independently of statistical significance.
Conclusion: progressive slowing of marathon performance as WBGT increases from 5 to 25 C, for men and women of wide ability, with slower runners affected more.
limitations: Compares placings with course records rather than within-athlete changes; sample size not stated; marathon road races only; WBGT does not separate humidity, sun and wind; no per-ability slope is given in the abstract.
implications: Add a weather adjustment: for top men about 0.9 percentage points of slowdown per 5 C WBGT (derived: 1.7% to 4.5% across quartile midpoints 7.5 to 22.5 C), larger for slower runners.
Scale the penalty up with predicted finish time; the abstract gives no multiplier.
Do not extrapolate below 5 C or above 25 C WBGT.
Use WBGT (not air temperature alone) as the weather input to a marathon-pace adjustment, with the 5-10 C WBGT band as the reference.

Reference penalty for top male finishers relative to the Q1 band (derived as differences of the reported means 1.7/2.5/3.3/4.5%): about +0.8% time at WBGT 10-15, +1.6% at 15-20 and +2.8% at 20-25. Slower finish-time groups slowed more but the abstract gives no figures, so the scale-up multiplier is a tunable default (grade D).
Do not extrapolate beyond WBGT 25 C; flag race-day plans above that as outside this evidence base.
Note the 10-15 C band already shows +0.8% here while Mantzios 2022 calls 7.5-15 C optimal; keep the band edges as tunable parameters.

verification.notes: Crossref and PubMed abstract re-fetched; quartile values match. The per-5 C slope is my arithmetic. Evidence level C kept; no sample count is stated.
